messages:
Priya (product): Heads-up from MercuryBank pilot: they want an "escape-hatch" playbook for evidence exports if keys or retention policies need emergency overrides. Requesting a short ops + legal flow + keystore escrow options before Dedicated onboarding. Can we map into a prioritized checklist?
Dmitri (eng-runtime): Quick: tech pieces = signed export manifest + signer_key_version + RFC3161 timestamp + immutable storage marker when legal-hold is active. For escape-hatch: we should support an emergency restore token flow (audited), not exposing private keys.
Helen (security): Important: define threat scenarios: lost tenant key, compromised key, legal subpoena requiring handed-over plaintext. Options: 1) tenant-managed KMS (no root access), 2) third-party escrow (multi-party), 3) Redwood temporary escrow with HSM-protected symmetric wrapping and strict audit + time-limited release. For verification over time include key history and signed key rotation records.
Omar (ops): Ops asks: 1) runbook for escape-hatch with roles (oncall, se/legal approval, SRE exec), 2) rate limits and audit logs for emergency exports, 3) guardrails: require dual-approval and time-limited signed release token. We should also define SLA for emergency export (e.g., target 8h after approvals).
Priya (product): Proposed pilot checklist (MUST): a) signed export manifest w/ per-file sha256 and signer_id/key_version; b) retention lanes + legal-hold; c) documented escape-hatch runbook with dual-approval; d) escrow options enumerated in PRD; e) signed proof-of-delivery. SHOULD: HSM attestation for Redwood-held keys, time-stamped ledger for key history.
Dmitri (eng-runtime): Minimal manifest example for PRD:```yaml
format: tar.gz
files:
  - path: audit/2026-03.log
    sha256: abcd...
signer: projects/redwood-kms/keys/tenant1/versions/4
key_version: 4
signature: BASE64...
rfc3161_token: BASE64_TSA...
```
We'll add `escape_hatch_token` metadata when an emergency release is used.
Helen (security): Policy notes: emergency release requires (1) written customer consent or legal compulsion, (2) dual approval (legal + security), (3) recorded signed release token stored in audit logs, (4) post-incident rotation plan and notification. I'll draft an emergency release policy with threat model.
Omar (ops): Cost/scope: emergency exports may be heavy; propose paid rush lane for guaranteed <8h, otherwise best-effort. Also preservation: toggling legal-hold must flip storage immutability flags. I'll draft runbook steps and expected SLAs.
contracts-bot: Contracts: we need contract appendix for "emergency export" and "escrow handling" describing responsibilities, approval flow, and liability limits. We'll draft a template clause.
Priya (product): Action items: Dmitri -> add escape_hatch_token and proof-of-delivery fields to manifest prototype; Helen -> emergency release policy + verification checklist; Omar -> ops runbook + SLA options; contracts -> draft appendix. I'll collate into a 1-page playbook for the pilot and schedule a 30m sign-off.
Dmitri (eng-runtime): Will drop manifest prototype and an example CLI: `rw export create --tenant mbank --since 2026-01-01 --signed=asymmetric --escape-hatch=disabled` by EOD.
Helen (security): I'll include verification flow: verify signature, check key_version, validate timestamp, confirm release token present if emergency path used.
Omar (ops): I'll include approval matrix (who signs), timing expectations, and required evidence to unblock.
Priya (product): Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll spin up the playbook doc and ping for review.
